text: Found it: in `middleware/proxy.go`, `randomBalancer.Next` and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` index into `b.targets` unconditionally, so a balancer built with no targets (`NewRandomBalancer(nil)` / `NewRoundRobinBalancer(nil)`) panics (index out of range / divide by zero) instead of returning nil. I'm fixing both `Next` methods to return nil when there are no targets, and making `ProxyWithConfig` return 503 (ErrServiceUnavailable) instead of dereferencing a nil target. A subagent is applying and verifying the fix (including a full `go test ./...` run to make sure no existing test breaks).

bind.go bug fixed and verified: `DefaultBinder.bindData` assumed every map value was a single string, so binding form/query data into a `map[string][]string` panicked (`reflect.Value.SetMapIndex: value of type string is not assignable to type []string`). It now supports `map[string][]string` (full slice), keeps `map[string]string` (first value) and `map[string]interface{}`, and skips unsupported map element types instead of panicking. Full `go test ./...` is green.

context.go bug fixed and verified: `(*context).Scheme()` returned the first non-empty `X-Forwarded-Proto`/`X-Forwarded-Protocol`/`X-Url-Scheme` header verbatim, so an invalid value (e.g. "garbage") was returned instead of being ignored. It now only accepts values that are exactly `http` or `https`, falls through to `X-Forwarded-Ssl: on`, then to `IsTLS()`, then `http`. Verified with a table test covering the two named subtests (invalid proto + valid protocol -> https; all invalid -> http) plus the existing `TestContext_Scheme`; full `go test ./...` green.

On it: in `middleware/compress.go` the gzip response writer writes to the gzip stream (and thus emits gzip framing bytes into the underlying writer) even when the handler writes an empty body, while the deferred cleanup then removes `Content-Encoding` because `res.Size == 0` — leaving a corrupt response (non-empty body, no encoding header). A subagent is reproducing it with a `TestGzipEmpty`-style test and fixing the writer so empty bodies stay empty. ETA ~4 min.

Fixed and verified: `middleware/proxy.go` — `randomBalancer.Next` and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` indexed `b.targets` unconditionally, so a balancer built with no targets panicked (index out of range / integer divide by zero). Both now return nil when there are no targets (under the existing lock), and `ProxyWithConfig` returns `echo.ErrServiceUnavailable` (503) instead of dereferencing a nil target. Full `go test ./...` is green.

Status on the router.go bug: the router itself does not panic on non-routable paths (empty path, `*`, `//`, absolute-form, CONNECT all return 404/200 without crashing), so the remaining piece is the request-target handling in `Echo.ServeHTTP`/`GetPath` — a non-routable target such as `*` or an absolute-form URI should be rejected with 400 Bad Request rather than routed. A subagent is still narrowing this down and applying the minimal fix; I'll confirm as soon as it's in.

Status on the group.go bug: `Group.Add` already allocates a fresh combined middleware slice (`make` + two `append`s) before calling `echo.add`, so the aliasing/overwrite scenario in the report is not present in `Group.Add`. The same pattern is what `Echo.add`/`Any`/`Match` rely on, so a subagent is checking whether the leak happens instead when the same path is registered twice through `Group.Use`/`Group.Group` (where the group's own `middleware` slice can be appended into and shared). I'll report the confirmed root cause and fix shortly.
